quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 (January-December 2025) results (annual securities report): orders received JPY 672,618 million (+3.0% vs the prior-year reference figures), net sales JPY 660,724 million (+2.6%), a record, operating income JPY 100,816 million (+24.4%), ordinary income JPY 104,649 million (+24.1%) and net income attributable to owners of the parent JPY 78,096 million (+21.3%); operating income, ordinary income and net income were records for the fourth straight year. Operating margin 15.3% and ROE 18.4%. The company now excludes the FX revaluation of the opening order backlog from orders; excluding that effect (242, in 100 million yen) from the prior-year reference, orders grew 7.0%. Service sales were 1,766 (100 million yen) against a 1,600 target. (The prior fiscal year was a 9-month transition period after the year-end moved from March to December; growth rates are against aligned reference figures.)
quarterly_data.figure: orders JPY 672,618 million (+3.0%); net sales JPY 660,724 million (+2.6%); operating income JPY 100,816 million (+24.4%); OP margin 15.3%; ROE 18.4%

quarterly_data.signal: Management's analysis of FY2025: orders of 6,726 (100 million yen) fell short of the initial forecast of 7,000 because automotive customers temporarily delayed investment decisions, with some orders shifting in timing; management expects those projects as order opportunities from FY2026 and judges overall orders solid given its profitability-focused order selection. Net sales of 6,607 beat the initial forecast of 6,500 on smooth project progress in intralogistics and semiconductor production-line systems; operating income of 1,008 (above 1,000 for the first time) beat the initial 815 (12.5% margin), which management attributes to standardisation and fewer parts, tighter project and cost management including large projects, and pricing in line with the value provided.
quarterly_data.figure: orders 6,726 vs 7,000 forecast; sales 6,607 vs 6,500; operating income 1,008 vs 815 (100 million yen)

quarterly_data.signal: Management on US trade policy: the US was 1,697 (100 million yen), 26% of FY2025 sales (1,677, 30% in FY2024, the transition period). Intralogistics, automotive and airport systems are mostly produced in the US; semiconductor production-line systems are produced in Japan, Taiwan and South Korea and exported to the US, but in most contracts the customer is the importer, so the tariffs the group bears are extremely limited. Management cautions that US trade policy could affect customers' investment plans (country, amount, timing), mainly in automotive and semiconductors.
quarterly_data.figure: US sales 1,697 (100 million yen), 26% of sales

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity: investments to raise capacity in the focus markets completed in FY2025 - the new factory in Indiana, US, finished in October 2025 and roughly doubled US production capacity for intralogistics systems (about 2x), and the new factory in Telangana, India, finished in April 2025 (about 4x capacity). The company aims to turn these into early growth in orders and sales.

FY2025 capital expenditure JPY 33,322 million, mainly maintenance, upgrade and expansion of the parent's factory equipment and expansion of North American and Indian subsidiaries' factories. Planned facility: Shiga Works (Hino, Shiga) new factory construction and production equipment, total investment JPY 33,000 million, JPY 14,455 million already paid, started April 2023, completion scheduled for March 2028 (added capacity not stated). Growth-area investment (capex, R&D, human capital) was 748 (100 million yen) cumulatively over FY2024-FY2025, of which 484 in FY2025, against about 1,600 planned over FY2024-FY2027.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 capex JPY 33,322 million; Shiga Works JPY 33,000 million, completion March 2028

quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 R&D expenses JPY 13,195 million (Daifuku Co., Ltd. JPY 10,479 million; Clean Factomation JPY 411 million). Semiconductor production-line products: automation needs are rising in back-end advanced packaging as well as the front end, and the company is developing new transport and storage systems for the wide variety of items handled; at the leading edge of the front end it has added delivery results for 2nm fabs and is now developing products for 1.4nm lines that build in AI with high reliability and energy-saving technology. It developed a battery-powered OHT (overhead hoist transport) to cut power consumption and uses AI-based operation control to raise transport efficiency. Clean Factomation works closely with Korean semiconductor customers on more efficient nitrogen-purge storage systems and transport/storage equipment for back-end packaging.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 R&D JPY 13,195 million; 2nm fab deliveries; 1.4nm line products in development

quarterly_data.signal: Mid-term targets updated on February 12, 2026 (FY2025 margin and ROE far exceeded the original FY2027 goals): FY2027 (December 2027) net sales 8,000 (100 million yen, unchanged), operating margin 15.0% (from 11.5%), operating income 1,200 (from 920), ROE 17.0% (from 13.0%); 2030 long-term vision net sales 1 trillion yen (unchanged), operating margin 15.0% (from 12.5%), operating income 1,500 (from 1,250), ROE 17.0% (from 13.0%).
quarterly_data.figure: FY2027 net sales 8,000, OP 1,200 (100 million yen), OP margin 15.0%; 2030 OP 1,500

quarterly_data.signal: Management's view of the environment: generative AI is driving a sharp rise in semiconductor demand while governments promote domestic production for economic security, so semiconductor investment is active in every region, with aggressive back-end as well as front-end investment expected in FY2026; China continues investing for localisation. On competition, management states startups with specific technologies are entering as generative AI and robotics advance, low-priced Chinese companies are rising, and Japanese competitors combine their products with overseas advanced products. FY2026 priorities: faster development of AI and robotics (new research sites in Tokyo and Kyoto), growth in the US and India including possible M&A, and continued profitability improvement.
